title: Canonical exact inverse-image tensor comparison
statement: For a scheme morphism h : S → T and unbounded derived sheaves K,L, transport the canonical left-derived pullback tensor isomorphism [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] along Lh* ≅ D(h*) to define D(h*)(K ⊗ᴸ L) ≅ D(h*)K ⊗ᴸ D(h*)L, using the derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Tensoring two isomorphisms is the composite obtained by applying the tensor bifunctor in its first and then its second variable. These are the existing supportDerivedTensorIso and supportExactPullbackTensorIso constructions, relocated without change of names, signatures, or bodies from def-pur-supported-localization-comparisons; no new mathematical object is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0F1E; same canonical derived tensor comparison used in def-pur-supported-localization-comparisons; blueprint thm-asd-smooth-tensor proof paragraph 3 requires this exact-model transport.

proof.text: Apply the derived tensor bifunctor to an isomorphism in each variable. Compose the inverse exact/left-derived comparison at K tensor L with the canonical left-derived tensor comparison, then tensor the forward comparisons at K and L. This explicit composite is the unchanged existing definition. It exists also on empty schemes, zero coefficients and unbounded complexes, and requires no etaleness or quasi-compactness.

proof_origin: R6, 2026-10-25: relocation of two existing real definitions to remove the support/smooth-duality import cycle; definitions verbatim, no theorem or hole added.
